component.name: FujiNet Go Adam
component.summary: Self-contained Coleco ADAM with built-in FujiNet

description.p: A Coleco ADAM (and ColecoVision) with FujiNet built in: mount disk and data-pack images from TNFS servers or the local SD folder, configure everything through the embedded FujiNet web UI, and play with automatic gamepad support. For developers it includes a full debugger with breakpoints, stepping, instruction history, EOS/OS7 symbols, and live VDP table viewers.

screenshot.caption: A Coleco ADAM running with FujiNet built in

description.p: FujiNet is far quicker to talk to. Listing a directory in CONFIG used to stop between every entry, and an EOS cold boot paused for several seconds right after the bus reset. Neither happens on a real ADAM, and both were faults in how this emulator drove the AdamNet link rather than anything in FujiNet itself.

Directory entries now arrive about five times faster. Every FujiNet command was preceded by a probe asking the device whether it had a leftover response to discard; the device answers that probe in a way the probe could not interpret, so it always ran to its full timeout — a quarter of a second added to each entry. The probe is gone, as it is on real hardware, and command replies are now collected as soon as they arrive instead of on the next emulated frame.

Cold boot no longer stalls. The ADAM asks every bus address in turn who is there, and the addresses FujiNet does not answer for were each given the long grace period meant for a device that is present but still starting up. Once FujiNet has shown it is responding, silence from an address is now taken to mean nothing is attached, which is what it means.

The bundled FujiNet runtime moves back onto upstream master. The previous build came from force-mbedtls-3, a branch that was never merged, so the runtime had been standing still while upstream moved on. The Mbed TLS 3.x requirement it was branched for has landed, and the device-chain rework and the Drivewire cassette media format arrive with it.

Note: as in 0.7.10, this build does not carry the AdamNet device-spec padding fix. That fix is still not on the firmware's mainline, so N: opens on AdamNet can see the padding that follows the device spec — a GCAL day view in particular may come back empty. It returns once the AdamNet work is merged upstream.

The bundled FujiNet runtime moves to a firmware build that refuses to compile against Mbed TLS 4.x. That release removed the low-level crypto headers the runtime's TLS backend needs and split the rest into a separate library, so a machine whose system Mbed TLS had moved to 4.x could produce a build with broken TLS instead of a clear failure. The build now finds a 3.x install, or stops and says so.
It also picks up Gmail message composition and the merged calendar work.

Note: this build temporarily loses the AdamNet device-spec padding fix that 0.7.9 shipped. That fix has not yet landed on the firmware's mainline, so N: opens on AdamNet can again see the padding that follows the device spec — a GCAL day view in particular may come back empty. It returns once the AdamNet work is merged upstream.

Fixes N: opens on AdamNet carrying the padding that follows the device spec. The client libraries send a fixed-size command block, so the URL arrives with the rest of the field after it; the runtime now stops at the end of the string, as every other bus does. A protocol that reads the device spec byte for byte — the new CALENDAR, GCAL and ICAL protocols do — saw the padding as part of the URL, so a GCAL day view was fetched as a calendar named after its own date and came back empty.

The bundled FujiNet runtime moves up to the current firmware. The web UI gains an optional global password and an SD card file manager; N: gains the CALENDAR, GCAL and ICAL protocols; the CONFIG slot-assignment screen shows the right filenames again; opening an AdamNet network connection no longer crashes on a null device; and a zero-length app key write clears the key instead of failing.
The runtime also builds again on systems that ship Mbed TLS 4.x, which no longer carries the legacy crypto headers it needs.

The debugger's VDP tab gains a VRAM hex editor (read and poke bytes directly, addresses wrap at 16K), a decoded view of the registers and the table addresses each mode is actually fetching from, and a redrawn palette strip with a separate, labeled square per color.
The Linux release now ships .deb/.rpm/.tar.gz packages (via CPack) alongside the flatpaks, matching the sibling CoCo and Apple II desktop apps' own release process.

Fixes the FujiNet Configuration window being unreachable when another FujiNet-family process on the machine already held the web admin's port. It now binds a random free port each run instead of a fixed one.
Fixes the OneDrive and Google Drive Authorize buttons in the FujiNet configuration page, which silently did nothing: they now open in the system browser, which OAuth requires anyway.
macOS: the app now ships its own icon in the Dock, Finder and Launchpad instead of the generic bundle icon.

Removes a multi-second freeze while loading. When the drive missed a request it was left to time out, stalling the machine for five seconds before anything retried; the request is now re-sent promptly.
Windows: FujiNet now starts. The shipped runtime library pulled in two libraries that were not part of the download, so it failed to load and the ADAM booted to SmartWriter with no FujiNet at all.

Fixes disk and data-pack loading: a drive now reports itself busy while it positions on a block and serves the data when the guest asks again, as the hardware does. Titles whose loaders rely on that exchange — Donkey Kong Super Game among them — previously stopped part-way and drew their play screen with the wrong graphics mode and colours.
Fixes a duplicate block problem in the ADAMnet-over-IP transport that could corrupt block reads from FujiNet.
FujiNet now runs on Windows as well, the native debugger is available in every frontend, and the macOS build gained the standard application, Window and Settings menus.
